'''Tooga Jallissi Gral''' was a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] who lived during the [[Time/Legends|time]] after the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. In [[44 ABY]], a group of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Violation|attacked]] the [[Fountain of Ancients|Fountain of the Hutt Ancients]] on [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]], which the Hutts had sworn by [[Treaty of Vontor|treaty]] to protect in return for the [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinians]]' [[Slavery/Legends|servitude]]. The Hutts sent reinforcements as quickly as possible and the Sith were stopped, but not before they had taken samples of [[wintrium]] from the Fountain. Some Klatooinians viewed this as a failure on the Hutts' part to uphold the treaty, and businessman [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] were brought in to mediate the situation. They spoke with the Sith, led by [[Leeha Faal]], who claimed falsely that [[Vyn Holpur]] and the crew of the [[ChaseMaster]] [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] ''[[Starstalker]]'' had acted of their own accord; with the Klatooinian [[Council of Elders (Klatooinian)|Council of Elders]]; and with Gral, who was chosen as the Hutt representative.

Gral claimed that the Hutts had come to the Klatooinians' aid as fast as they could, and that, due to the great damages they had attained during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Hutts numbers were too few. Gral went on to say that he believed no one could have stopped the attack. Calrissian and Solo then decided that Holpur and his crew were guilty, and that, since the Fountain was violated, Gral did not precisely obey the treaty. However, they went on to say that the Hutts' inability to protect the Fountain during the sudden attack was not a direct dereliction of duty, because the Hutts could not have reasonably been expected to have foreseen the attack. Despite this ruling, several [[Liberation|uprisings]] began all over Klatooine, as the Klatooinians rebelled against their Hutt leadership.
